driving_question: Does the feed run on the same handkerchief - is the attention economy the conjurer's trick that makes the authentic and the artificial interchangeable and profitable, the white-rabbit mechanism that re-extracts the menace (the real crisis) as content (the engagement) when the audience is ready for the sequel? (q0097)
book: Information Doesn't Want to Be Free (Cory Doctorow, 2014)
best_collision: The same per-person ledger, inverted: c01933 - the lock-holder hoards the per-person stream accounting as a lump (Merlin's guarantee = six times the royalties, the labels keep it) vs c01946 - the Humble Bundle shows the donor the same accounting ('Windows users are giving an average of $40') and the fan pays more from competitive shame. The ledger is the handkerchief's engine: hoarded, it owns the audience; shown, it taxes the fan.
quote: You're on a Windows PC, and Windows users are giving an average of $40. Mac users are giving an average of $43, and Linux users are giving $48. (p.88)
mutation_note: The book finishes at the ceiling with the trick's answer to scarcity named as a change of species - the dandelion (seeds to the wind, no mourning) - and the direct wire's last node revealed as its own lock (PayPal freezes the account). The abundance economy does not end the lock, it reclassifies it: the seeds are the fans, and the fans pay more because they can see what the other fans pay.
